comparison: Perfect agreement on alpha modulation patterns (C23-C25). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find these foundational observations well-supported, with OpenEval noting replication of prior work and peer reviewers accepting the findings without critique.

Perfect agreement on subcortical asymmetry characterization (C26-C32). Both evaluations accept the volumetric lateralization findings. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical testing but mentions lack of explicit multiple comparison correction; peer reviewers do not raise concerns about these measurements.

Perfect agreement on null findings (C40). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the negative results for behavioral and RIFT correlations. OpenEval emphasizes the importance of these null findings for delimiting subcortical contributions; peer reviewers do not contest these results.

Agreement on model validation approach (C41-C42). Both evaluations support the multivariate multiple regression framework. OpenEval finds the model comparison appropriate for demonstrating specificity; peer reviewers implicitly accept this framework while raising concerns about condition-specific testing elsewhere.

Strong agreement on core findings (C3, C36-C39). Both evaluations support the main correlation between subcortical asymmetries and alpha lateralization. OpenEval notes appropriate model selection and significant predictive power with marginal globus pallidus effect; peer reviewers affirm this as the core finding with 'convincing' strength of evidence.

Significant disagreement on condition-specific effects (C4, C43-C52). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to marginal p-values and low statistical power but finds the pattern plausible. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN with stronger concerns, explicitly questioning the statistical approach for establishing specificity and noting difficulty following the rationale, describing results as 'post hoc' with inadequate power for direct comparisons.

OpenEval evaluates the conceptual framework and literature justification (C60, C53-C59) as SUPPORTED, finding reasonable justification from cited studies on experience-dependent plasticity and subcortical-cognitive relationships. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this theoretical framing.

OpenEval evaluates contextualization relative to prior work (C65) as SUPPORTED, noting replication of globus pallidus effects strengthens generalizability despite marginal significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparison to prior literature.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretations (C66-C73) as SUPPORTED but speculative, noting plausible explanations for thalamic relay, GABAergic inhibition, and caudate involvement grounded in literature but acknowledging these remain interpretations of correlational findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates conclusions about mechanism from null RIFT findings (C77) as UNCERTAIN, noting the inference about 'downstream gating' versus 'gain control' is speculative and could reflect power or methodological limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific mechanistic claim.

OpenEval evaluates methodological approach (C78-C97) as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable sample size and validated tools but identifying multi-scanner MRI data as a notable limitation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific methodological details.
